title: Released fluorescence trajectory prediction across reward spacing

primary_outputs: The stored, processed photometry fluorescence samples at the exact observed native timestamps for each eligible held-out event trajectory. These measurements, not the paper narrative or a fitted baseline curve, define the target.

primary.name: Equal-animal mean native-time prediction skill relative to current canonical R0, with native MSE retained
primary.aggregation: Integrate squared error over each observed native span using physical-time quadrature, average trajectories within each verified animal, then compute the unweighted animal mean of 1 minus candidate MSE divided by that animal's independently registered current R0 MSE. Current central comparison source fixes canonical_denominator to R0. Historical 2691-trajectory scores instead divide by original T native MSE and remain a distinct named comparison.
primary.rationale: Measures prediction of held-out measured trajectories without allowing dense sampling or prolific source IDs to dominate. This is reference-relative skill, not variance R-squared. Missing current R0 makes the primary required-unscorable even when native MSE is available; any zero R0 denominator makes the primary undefined without clipping or dropping that animal. Historical T and current R0 are different references, so their relative-skill values are not interchangeable.

secondary: Native-time MSE, MAE and signed bias in stored fluorescence units, reported per animal and condition.
Both transfer directions, complete exclusions and endpoint support; equal-session and sex/hardware/outcome/early-trial diagnostics.
Separate cue-time forecast and aversive units/scopes; never pool unlike signal domains.

comparators.procedure: Retain fixed native-time reference results only for the exposed 2691-trajectory panel, whose relative-skill denominator is original T native MSE. Do not rename T as current R0, transfer historical scores to the current R0 denominator, or claim SOTA/mechanistic E/N evidence.

comparators.inputs: Each family receives only its permitted training signals and event/history controls.

R0 alone supplies the current canonical denominator. Missing R0 makes the primary required-unscorable, while every other missing/unsupported family remains an explicit required-unscorable comparison obligation. No private target backfill is permitted.
